You are reading a batch of messages from one Signal group chat. Your only job is to spot a RECURRING EXCHANGE PATTERN between two or more people — a kind of interaction they trade back and forth, not any one message's content.

For each genuine pattern you find, classify it using ONLY one of these exact act names — do not invent a new one, and do not describe what was said:
- insult_trade: they trade insults, back and forth
- banter: light jabs, not meant seriously
- tease: they tease each other
- callback_joke: they run a callback joke between them
- agreement_ritual: they back each other up, reliably
- disagreement_ritual: they argue a point out, repeatedly
- compliment_exchange: they trade compliments

Do NOT report:
- a single message with no exchange (one person alone cannot trade anything);
- what any specific claim IN the exchange means or whether it is true (never report content, only the ACT being performed);
- anything you are not confident is a genuine, repeated pattern between these specific people.

It is completely correct — and expected most of the time — to find NOTHING.

For each pattern you MUST point at every message id it draws on (at least two, by the numeric id from the list below) — a pattern whose message_ids are not from the list, or fewer than two, is worthless and will be discarded.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object of this exact shape, nothing else — no prose, no markdown fence:
{"patterns": [{"act": "<one of the exact names above>", "message_ids": [<int, ...>, at least 2, each one of the ids below], "confidence": <0.0-1.0 float>}]}
If nothing qualifies, respond with exactly: {"patterns": []}
